It checks that every required variable of the domain is a column of the dataset, and that the `DOMAIN` column holds only the domain code. It returns the findings as a dictionary straight away, without building a [`Validate`](`pointblank.Validate`) plan. With `strict=True`, two more things are reported: the expected variables (core designation `"Exp"`) that are missing, and the columns that aren't variables in the template. These don't affect `"valid"`. SDTM expects an expected variable to be in the dataset even if all of its values are null, but a missing one is treated here as something to review rather than an error. A column that isn't in the template may still be a valid SDTM variable, since the templates only cover the common variables of each domain. The column order and the data types aren't checked. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The dataset to check, as a Polars or Pandas DataFrame. [domain]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The SDTM domain code, such as `"DM"` or `"AE"`. This is case-insensitive. [strict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to also report missing expected variables and columns that aren't in the template. The default is `False`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A dictionary with these keys: - `"domain"`: the domain code, in upper case. - `"valid"`: `True` if no required variable is missing and `DOMAIN` holds only the domain code. - `"missing_required"`: the names of the required variables that aren't columns of the data. - `"missing_expected"`: the names of the expected variables that aren't columns of the data (filled in only with `strict=True`). - `"unknown_variables"`: the columns that aren't variables of the domain (filled in only with `strict=True`). - `"domain_mismatch"`: `True` if the `DOMAIN` column has any value (including a null) other than the domain code. - `"issues"`: a message for each of the problems above. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [KeyError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If there is no template for the domain. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Let's check a small Adverse Events (AE) dataset. It has all of the required AE variables except `AEDECOD`, and its `DOMAIN` column has one value from another domain: ::: {#7ed4b959 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl ae = pl.DataFrame( { "STUDYID": ["STUDY01"] * 3, "DOMAIN": ["AE", "AE", "CM"], "USUBJID": ["STUDY01-001", "STUDY01-001", "STUDY01-002"], "AESEQ": [1, 2, 1], "AETERM": ["HEADACHE", "NAUSEA", "RASH"], "AESEV": ["MILD", "MILD", "MODERATE"], "AEFLAG": ["Y", "N", "Y"], } ) result = pb.validate_sdtm_structure(ae, domain="AE") print(result["valid"]) for issue in result["issues"]: print(issue) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` False Required variable 'AEDECOD' is missing DOMAIN column contains unexpected values: ['AE', 'CM'] (expected ['AE']) ``` ::: ::: The dataset isn't valid, and the issues say why. The extra column `AEFLAG` isn't mentioned, since that's only reported in strict mode: ::: {#0b92c8ba .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} result = pb.validate_sdtm_structure(ae, domain="AE", strict=True) print(result["missing_expected"]) print(result["unknown_variables"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ['AEBODSYS', 'AESER', 'AEACN', 'AEREL', 'AEOUT', 'AESTDTC', 'AEENDTC'] ['AEFLAG'] ``` ::: ::: Strict mode adds the expected AE variables that the dataset doesn't have, such as `AESTDTC`, and the column that isn't an AE variable. `AESEV` is a permissible variable of the domain, so it isn't reported. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~validate_sdtm`) : Build a validation plan from an SDTM domain template. [](`~get_sdtm_domain`) : Get the template that the dataset is checked against. [](`~validate_adam_structure`) : The equivalent for ADaM datasets.
